edits.rationale: Cloud Cost Room advises setting min/max tiers based on steady-state demand and reviewing scale events because a spike can leave a cluster on a permanently higher tier. MongoDB's own auto-scaling docs say the min/max range helps control costs and advise sizing the minimum for expected workload. The caveat that this is guidance and not a hard billing cap is the pack's own framing and is consistent with the sources.

edits.old: If a smaller tier cannot support existing disk capacity or provisioned IOPS, Atlas Core refuses the downgrade. At the configured maximum it disables automatic downscaling; otherwise it raises the minimum to the current tier without disabling downward scaling. Storage growth can also make the former minimum invalid. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

evidence.quote: If Atlas attempts to scale your cluster tier down and the target tier can't support your current disk capacity, provisioned IOPS (Input/Output Operations per Second), or both, Atlas doesn't scale your cluster down.
If the cluster is currently at the configured maximum cluster tier, Atlas disables the cluster from automatically scaling down
If the cluster isn't currently at the configured maximum cluster tier, Atlas raises the minimum cluster tier to the current cluster tier. In this case, Atlas doesn't disable downward auto-scaling.

If your storage increases beyond what is supported by your minimum cluster tier, and Atlas increases your clusters storage configuration beyond what your minimum cluster tier supports, then Atlas automatically adjusts your minimum cluster tier

statements.statement: If a smaller tier cannot support existing disk capacity or provisioned IOPS, Atlas Core refuses the downgrade.

statements.note: Compute page: Atlas automatically adjusts the minimum tier when storage outgrows it (the page's example says M20 is 'no longer a valid auto-scaling bound').

edits.rationale: The Atlas storage page states the refused downgrade and the two outcomes (at the maximum: downward scaling disabled; otherwise: minimum raised, downward scaling kept). The Atlas compute page states that storage growth beyond what the minimum tier supports makes Atlas adjust the minimum tier. Together these establish every statement.

The `lifecycle.ignore_changes` block prevents Terraform from reverting these Atlas-managed changes.
